flows:
Navigate to http://localhost:3000/examples/waitlist then Open the page.
Type "tester@provewall.dev" into the email input.
Click the "Sign up" button.
Confirm a success message containing "You're on the list" appears on the page.

remark: type: Typing tester@provewall.dev in email address field
click: Clicking Sign up button below the email input
wait: PRIMARY: wait 1000 ms for the waitlist success message to appear
press_key: PRIMARY: press the Enter key

summary:
After submitting the form, the automation assumed the success message would appear right away. When it did not see that state quickly, it tried an extra Enter press and then ran out of useful actions.
Update the test to handle the post-submit state more carefully: wait longer, check for loading or validation feedback, and capture any visible error text before deciding the app is stuck.
one_liner: The browser run broke because it expected the page to move into a success state, but after a short wait it had no reliable next step and stalled.
reason: AP determined agent is stuck — no viable actions remain

verdict.root_cause: After submitting the form, the automation assumed the success message would appear right away. When it did not see that state quickly, it tried an extra Enter press and then ran out of useful actions.
verdict.agent_fault_assessment: The agent used the correct field and button, so there is no sign it clicked or typed into the wrong element. However, the run still ended because the automation only waited briefly for the result, then sent an extra Enter key, and finally got stuck without collecting evidence of an application error. That means the failure was caused by the test flow running out of recovery steps, not by a proven product defect.
verdict.bug_title: Waitlist signup check gives up before confirming submission result
verdict.suggestion: Update the test to handle the post-submit state more carefully: wait longer, check for loading or validation feedback, and capture any visible error text before deciding the app is stuck.
